**Stained Glass**, the module's new look, opt-out. The interface is one sheet of broken black stained glass along the screen edges: the clock, the Despair rail, the status strip, the Projects tray and the launchers each sit on their own pane of it, colour lives in the seams and in a few tinted panes, and the glass breathes - every pane darkens towards black and comes back on its own slow rhythm, the way the trial screen in Danganronpa V3 does. The design page with every number is in `docs/design/identity-audit-v13.html`.

## Themes

- A **Theme** setting, per browser: **Stained Glass** (default) or **Monokuma Legacy**, which is the look of 1.2.14, unchanged. Two more client settings beside it: **Glass effects** (the blur and the pulse) and **Interface scale** (80 to 140 percent, the map is never scaled).
- Two faces ship with the module under the OFL: VT323 for chrome, prose and stamps, Special Elite for titles. Latin and latin-ext, so Polish names render in one face. Rules for both are in `docs/design/typography.md`.

## The screen

- The curtain is cut for the module's own layout and checked after every cut: no two panes overlap, every piece is convex, every block lies inside its own pane, the frame is continuous along all four edges. Foundry's scene controls and sidebar tabs sit on a shard of their own, turned parallel to its straight edge.
- The seam colour follows the hour and the phase (Investigation, Class Trial, Eclipse). When either changes, every seam flashes Bone for a beat and the glass takes the new colour; the shape never changes.
- The sound launcher is now the **Settings** launcher (a gear): volumes, theme, glass effects, scale, all this browser's own. The GM's Sound window keeps its playlists and effects and loses the sliders.
- Module windows carry the glass on their title band only; the body is calm dark glass. The character sheet has two materials: the left column on matt ink with the module's raster, the header on a glass band. The pause band is a pane of the curtain.

## The Event panel

- A narrow panel under the Despair rail, as wide as it, with no button in it. It takes the rows the clock used to carry: Monokuma's motive, a deferred assembly, the open incident, and whose floor it is in the Class Trial. The clock is a clock again.
- The incident card is shown to its participants and to the GM, and to nobody else - a spectator's screen shows no card at all.

## Motion

- Light moves on the seams, elements stand still. Waiting states (a pending Despair Call, a motive that is due, the objection on the clock) glow at the seam instead of fading; the window entrance keeps its fade and drops the scale. Everything stops under reduced motion or with Glass effects off, and the pulse does not run in a hidden tab.

## Known and to verify at the table

- The glass under the side tiles may need a little reshaping once seen on a live client; the geometry is parametric for that (`wTop`, `wCtl`, `yCtl` in `docs/design/glass-recipe.js`, ported by `tools/port-glass.py`).
- Interface scale works through `zoom` on `#interface`; check the two extremes with a few windows open.

Under Monokuma Legacy nothing in this release changes what you see.
